analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject, and אֶת marks רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ, “the pleasing aroma,” as the direct object of וַיָּרַח.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּרַח יַהְוֶה אֶת רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ, יַהְוֶה names the one who smelled the pleasing aroma. The verb וַיָּרַח is masculine singular, and אֶת marks the aroma as its object.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject of וַיָּרַח ‘smelled’. אֶת introduces רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ ‘the pleasing aroma’, the definite construct phrase naming what he smelled.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּרַח יַהְוֶה אֶת רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ, רֵיחַ heads the phrase marked by אֶת as the object of וַיָּרַח, “smelled.” The full phrase means “the pleasing aroma.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ, “the soothing aroma,” רֵיחַ is the construct noun and הַנִּיחֹחַ names the quality of the scent. Yahweh smells the aroma and resolves never again to strike every living thing as he has done.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: soothing quality of an offering’s scent

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject. אֶל לִבּוֹ (‘to his heart’) shows that he speaks to himself, and לֹא אֹסִף (‘I will not again …’) begins the direct quotation of his resolve.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל לִבּוֹ, “Yahweh said to himself,” יַהְוֶה names the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר and identifies the speaker of the promise that follows.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל לִבּוֹ, אֶל marks the addressee of וַיֹּאמֶר. Yahweh speaks “to his heart,” that is, to himself.
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל לִבּוֹ, “Yahweh said to himself,” the suffix refers to Yahweh. His words express his resolve never again to curse the ground or strike down every living thing as he had done.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: Yahweh’s own heart: his mind and purpose

analysis.evidence: In לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, “I will not curse the ground again,” לֹא negates the first-person verb אֹסִף. The speaker declares his own future course of action.
analysis.morphology: Negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד, the infinitive לְקַלֵּל names the action and עוֹד reinforces repetition. Yahweh says, “I will never again curse the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, first person common singular

analysis.evidence: לְקַלֵּל complements לֹא אֹסִף, and אֶת הָאֲדָמָה marks the ground as its direct object. YHWH resolves never again to curse the ground on account of humankind.
analysis.morphology: Piel infinitive construct with prefixed לְ

analysis.evidence: In לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, עוֹד marks a further act of cursing. The negative לֹא rules out its repetition: “I will never again curse the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again

analysis.evidence: In לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, אֶת marks הָאֲדָמָה (“the ground”) as the definite direct object of לְקַלֵּל (“to curse”).
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאֲדָמָה as the object of לְקַלֵּל, “to curse.” The promise to refrain from cursing the ground on humankind’s account recalls the curse on the soil in Genesis 3:17.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ plus feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil

analysis.evidence: In לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם, the ground is what is cursed, and בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם identifies humanity as the reason for the curse.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בַּ־ with masculine singular construct עֲבוּר, together functioning as a compound preposition governing הָאָדָם.
analysis.sense: for the sake of, on account of, because of

analysis.evidence: בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם means “on account of humankind.” The following clause explains this by describing the inclination of the human heart from youth, giving הָאָדָם collective reference.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with the definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason YHWH gives for his resolve never again to curse the ground on humanity’s account: the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: יֵצֶר heads the construct chain יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם, “the inclination of the human heart.” The predicate רַע describes that inclination as evil, and מִנְּעֻרָיו places it from youth onward.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם, “the inclination of the human heart,” לֵב is in construct with הָאָדָם. The words רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו describe that inclination as evil from youth, identifying the heart as the source of human inclinations.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם, “the inclination of the human heart,” הָאָדָם completes the construct chain. The statement that this inclination is evil מִנְּעֻרָיו, “from his youth,” describes humans generally.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with the definite article הָ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: רַע agrees with יֵצֶר, the masculine singular head of יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם. The clause says that the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively.
analysis.sense: evil, wicked (of persons, hearts, ways, deeds)

analysis.evidence: In יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו, the suffix refers to הָאָדָם, the human being. The preposition marks youth as the time from which the inclination of the human heart is described as evil.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition מִן with its final נ assimilated to the noun’s initial נ; plural noun in construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: youth, the early years of a life

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא אֹסִף עוֹד לְהַכּוֹת, the infinitive לְהַכּוֹת names the action and עוֹד reinforces repetition: “and I will never again strike.” כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי (“as I did”) identifies the earlier act.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, first person common singular, with first-person prefix אֹ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא אֹסִף עוֹד לְהַכּוֹת, the negation governs the whole phrase, “and I will never again strike.” כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי (“as I have done”) identifies the earlier act whose repetition is ruled out.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again

analysis.evidence: אֶת־כָּל־חַי identifies every living thing as the object of לְהַכּוֹת. The closing כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי (“as I have done”) recalls the deaths in the flood and gives the verb its lethal force.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ

analysis.evidence: In לְהַכּוֹת אֶת כָּל חַי, “to strike every living thing,” אֶת marks כָּל חַי as the direct object of לְהַכּוֹת.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object marker without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לְהַכּוֹת אֶת כָּל חַי, כָּל quantifies the singular חַי, “living thing.” The phrase means “to strike every living thing.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לְהַכּוֹת אֶת כָּל חַי, “to strike every living thing,” חַי stands without an expressed noun. כָּל gives it universal scope, and אֶת marks the whole phrase as the object of “strike.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי means “as I did.” It compares striking every living thing with what God did before.
analysis.morphology: Relative particle with prefixed comparative preposition כַּ.
analysis.sense: with a preposition: as, where, than, until

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי means “as I did.” The preceding לְהַכּוֹת אֶת כָּל חַי identifies the action the speaker recalls, striking every living thing.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular, with subject ending ־תִי.
